channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: FIDE Elects Its President in Samarkand: Three Tickets and ~200 Federation Votes
item.description: The vote falls on 26 September at the FIDE General Assembly held alongside the 46th Chess Olympiad. Incumbent Arkady Dvorkovich suspended his powers in July after EU sanctions.

item.title: Pax Silica vs WAICO: Kazakhstan Is in Both AI Blocs, Uzbekistan Has Applied
item.description: Kazakhstan joined the US-led Pax Silica initiative on 25 June and China's WAICO on 16 July. Reuters reported that Washington is preparing to ask dozens of countries to choose.

item.title: EU–Uzbekistan: EPCA in Force Since 1 March, GSP+ Rules Change in 2027
item.description: The Enhanced Partnership and Cooperation Agreement was signed on 24 October 2025 and has been provisionally applied since 1 March 2026. Requirements under the EU's preferential trade scheme tighten next year.

item.title: Seoul Hosts the First Central Asia–Republic of Korea Summit
item.description: On September 16 President Lee Jae Myung received the leaders of all five Central Asian states. A cooperation forum that had run at ministerial level since 2007 was raised to the level of heads of state; a Seoul Declaration was set to be adopted.

item.title: Karachaganak Halts for Maintenance: Kazakh Output to Fall by up to 450,000 Tonnes
item.description: The field is under planned maintenance from 7 September to 1 October. Kazakhstan had already cut its 2026 oil plan from 98 to 96 million tonnes because of attacks on CPC infrastructure.

item.title: Labour Migration From Central Asia to Russia Falls 15%; Kyrgyzstan Down 16.7%
item.description: Russian border-service data show work-related entries by citizens of three Central Asian states fell from 2.3 million to 1.9 million in the first half of 2026. Kyrgyzstan recorded 289,100 entries.

item.title: Uzbekistan Relists Unsold State Assets at ~$83 Opening Bids
item.description: 84 state assets that found no buyer for years will be re-auctioned at a starting price of just 1 million soum (~$83). The required down payment is cut from 35% to 15%.

item.title: Is the Hijab Banned in Kazakhstan? The School Ban and the Secularism Debate
item.description: Short answer: there is no blanket ban — but in schools the hijab is prohibited under uniform rules. That restriction has sparked fierce debate over secularism and religious freedom in Kazakhstan.

item.title: China Becomes Central Asia's Top Trade Partner — Russia Left Behind
item.description: In 2025, China–Central Asia trade crossed $100 billion for the first time, hitting a record $106.3 billion. China became the region's largest trade partner for the first time.

item.title: Tokayev Meets US Envoy at BRICS — Trump Sends a Personal Message
item.description: On the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi, Kazakh President Tokayev met US Special Envoy Sergio Gor, who conveyed a personal message from President Trump.

item.title: Why Is Uzbekistan Losing Its Women Engineers?
item.description: Women engineers are leaving the profession — especially in the energy sector — under family pressure, hiring barriers and poor workplace conditions. The attrition starts at the education stage.

item.title: The Largest Chess Olympiad in History in Samarkand: 400 Teams, 1,980 Players
item.description: The 46th Chess Olympiad will be held in Samarkand from Sept. 15 to 27. According to FIDE, the number of participating teams is 20 more than the 2024 record in Budapest. Uzbekistan's men's team starts as the third seed.

item.title: Houthis Seize Two More Strategic Islands in the Red Sea; Saudi Arabia Carries Out Strikes
item.description: The Greater and Lesser Hanish islands have been brought under control. Roughly 12 percent of world trade passes through the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

item.title: Mahmoud Khalil Files Suit Against Columbia University, Alleging Failure to Protect Students From Doxxing
item.description: The complaint was filed in federal court in Manhattan on Sept. 14. It accuses the university of failing to protect students harassed because of their Arab or Muslim background.

item.title: Nearly 100,000 Uzbeks Returned From Russia in 10 Days
item.description: According to the Migration Agency, 96,415 citizens returned home between Aug. 25 and Sept. 5 — against the backdrop of Russia's tightening migration policy.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Sign 13 Documents in Seoul
item.description: Talks between Mirziyoyev and Lee Jae-myung concluded with an exchange of cooperation documents on critical minerals, artificial intelligence and defense. The meeting came on the eve of the first Korea–Central Asia summit on Sept. 16.

item.title: Conference of Central Asian Women Journalists in Tashkent: A Regional Program Through 2029 Under Discussion
item.description: The second conference, held Sept. 14–15, brought together more than 100 journalists and media managers from five countries. The main themes were digital security and deepfakes.

item.title: Indian Company Brings Gold Mine Online in Kyrgyzstan: $34.2 Million Spent on the Altyn Tor Project
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov opened the processing plant in an online ceremony on Sept. 13. The project is expected to create close to 400 jobs.

item.title: Strikes Continue in Gaza: Two Killed on Sept. 13, Hospital Generators Shut Down
item.description: A vehicle was struck in the Tal al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City on Sept. 13. According to the Health Ministry, hospital generators have failed because of a fuel shortage. The total death toll has reached 73,669.

item.title: Javokhir Sindarov Outscores Carlsen and Nepomniachtchi at the Global Chess League
item.description: At the tournament held in Bengaluru from Sept. 5 to 13, the Uzbek grandmaster scored the most points on the Icon board. His team finished third overall.

item.title: Pezeshkian at the BRICS Summit: “Unilateral Sanctions Directly Affect Food Security”
item.description: At the summit in New Delhi, Iran's president called for expanding trade in national currencies and said international mechanisms need reform.

item.title: CSTO “Rubezh-2026” Exercises Begin in Kazakhstan, With a Cross-Border Incursion as the Main Scenario
item.description: From Sept. 12 to 19, rapid deployment forces are training in mountain and desert conditions at the Koktal range in the Zhetysu region.

item.title: BRICS Adopts New Delhi Declaration: 140 Paragraphs on UN Reform and AI Governance
item.description: The 18th BRICS summit was held Sept. 12–13 under India's chairmanship. The declaration addressed tensions in the Middle East, reform of the UN Security Council, unilateral sanctions and settlements in national currencies.

item.title: Tokayev Meets U.S. Special Envoy Sergio Gor on the Sidelines of the BRICS Summit
item.description: Cooperation in artificial intelligence and digitalization was discussed at the Sept. 12 meeting in New Delhi. Gor conveyed Donald Trump's personal congratulations; Tokayev reiterated his invitation for Trump to visit Kazakhstan.

item.title: Elena Rybakina Beats Sabalenka in the US Open Final and Becomes World No. 1
item.description: The Kazakh player won 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 in the final in New York on Sept. 12. It is her third Grand Slam title.

item.title: Mirziyoyev and Pashinyan Hold Phone Call: Trade Up 2.1-Fold Over Seven Months
item.description: The Sept. 11 conversation covered industrial cooperation and the unblocking of regional communications.

item.title: 25 Years Since 9/11: The New York Ceremony and the Debate Over Muslim Americans
item.description: Four former presidents attended the memorial service at Ground Zero. The presence of Zohran Mamdani, the city's first Muslim mayor, drew debate of its own.

item.title: A $350 Million Fuel Processing Complex Is Being Built in the Talas Region
item.description: On Sept. 11, Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy and the Kazakh company QAZAQ BITUM Processing signed a memorandum of intent.

item.title: Uzbekistan–Japan Economic Committees Meet in Tashkent: A Portfolio of 75 Projects Worth $12 Billion
item.description: More than 130 Japanese participants attended the 18th meeting. The priority areas are energy, chemicals, machine building, critical minerals, health care and IT.

item.title: PISA 2025 Results: Uzbekistan Leads the Region in Science, Kazakhstan's Math Score Declines
item.description: In the OECD study, Uzbekistan posted the highest result in Central Asia with 438 points, a gain of 83 points over 2022 — the largest jump among all participants.
